CHIEF COMPLAINT
Big toe pain and redness for two weeks, worsening over the past week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports intermittent pain in his big toe for approximately two weeks, with significant worsening last week during a trade show convention where he was unable to walk the halls comfortably. The pain is described as throbbing with occasional sharp stabbing quality, particularly with movement or prolonged walking. Patient reports walking on his heel to minimize toe bending. Pain worsens with light pressure, including from bed sheets at night. The toe became red and warm to the touch, which prompted him to seek care. Patient denies a specific injury. He takes ibuprofen 200mg twice daily without significant relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports that even light pressure bothers the toe, including contact with bed sheets at night. Pain is exacerbated by walking and toe motion. Denies stomach problems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 200mg twice daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a job requiring him to be on his feet daily. He enjoys biking on trails and reports putting in over 800 miles on trails in the past year. He rides bikes with regular shoes on regular pedals and often wears flip-flops. He also enjoys fishing and running. He enjoys spicy Mexican food.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals redness and warmth of the big toe. Palpation elicits pain with range of motion testing. Plantar flexion causes pain, with 10 degrees causing mild discomfort and 20 degrees causing more pain. Dorsiflexion causes pain but less than plantar flexion. Medial-lateral motion causes pain with a grinding sensation noted. Pain elicited with palpation on the lateral (outside) aspect of the toe. A bone spur is palpated on the dorsal aspect of the big toe joint.

RESULTS
X-ray of the foot reveals a large spur on the dorsal aspect of the big toe joint with significant loss of cartilage, consistent with arthritis (hallux rigidus).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus with osteoarthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Plan includes: (1) Custom foot orthotic insert for shoe; (2) Meloxicam once daily for anti-inflammatory effect, with patient counseled to discontinue and call if heartburn or substernal pain develops; (3) Patient instructed to continue regular work and activities to allow for proper assessment of treatment efficacy; (4) Follow-up appointment in two weeks to assess response to treatment; (5) If inadequate improvement, consider more invasive options including corticosteroid injection or surgical intervention (joint cleaning or arthrodesis).
